newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Despite wage hike Gengold lifts Q3 profit.
newsitem.headline: Despite wage hike Gengold lifts Q3 profit.

text.p: Despite wage increases and a higher tax bill, Gencor Ltd's gold division Gengold lifted third quarter distributable income by a slight 1.8 percent to 57.4 million rand.
Gengold managing director Tom Dale said at the results presentation on Monday that gold output rose six percent to 10,104 kg -- including 437 kg from its developing Oryx mine.
"I think another important thing is that Oryx produced 437 kg of gold and that took Gengold over the 10 tonne (of gold produced) mark for the quarter.

"It is the fifth consecutive quarter that we have an increase in distributable (income) and I think the major beneficiary of that this time was the receiver (of revenue) because we paid 50 percent more tax," Dale said.
The company's tax bill increased to 5.82 million rand from 3.89 million in the June quarter.
Dale said Gengold paid wage increases of around nine percent -- backdated to July 1 under an agreement between the Chamber of Mines and the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM).

Gengold's St Helena Gold Mines Ltd -- which faced closure six months ago -- turned in a strong performance, lifting bottom-line distributable income by 60 percent to 6.6 million rand from 4.14 million in the second quarter.
Dale said the mine showed an improvement in all aspects of its business although working costs increased, mainly as a result of higher wages.
Winkelhaak Mines Ltd broke into profit, posting a distributable income of 12,000 rand after reporting a 6.8 million rand loss in the June quarter.
Dale said that the benefits of the mine's rationalisation process were beginning to show.
Beatrix Mines increased distributable income to 37.4 million rand from 34.4 million, but working costs increased during the quarter to 30,905 rand/kg from 28,434 rand/kg.
Still, Dale said that Beatrix's working costs -- the lowest in the industry -- were better than target.
"It is above target but I think the cost level at 118 million rand is 10 million above the previous quarter. A lot of that is pay increases," he said.
Dale said Gengold was actively trying to increase the mine's resource base.
"We are talking to all the mineral rights holders to the north of Beatrix," he said. "There are substantial resources to the north of Beatrix."
Gengold said that the No. 3 shaft expansion project at Beatrix remained on schedule and the metallurgical plant was commissioned last month.
Borehole drilling and development at Oryx, a division of St Helena, continued to show in situ values above those upon which the decision to fund the mine was based.
"We are maintaining values in excess of that level, both in development and in borehole drilling," Dale said.
"We expect the level of gold output in the December quarter to be something similiar to that which we achieved this quarter," he added.
Total operating income for Beatrix, Kinross Mines Ltd, Leslie Gold Mines Ltd, St Helena and Winkelhaak increased by 3.6 percent to 116 million rand.
